slides.title: Used Oil Storage
slides.description:
• Above ground tanks with capacity of 660 gallons or more are subject to federal regulations
  • Collection drums must be covered and labeled, in good condition and secured from vandals, and in compliance with local fire codes.
  • Inspect weekly for leaks, corrosion or spillage
  • Label drums, tanks and fill pipes with the wordsUsed Oil
  • No Smokingsigns should be posted in used oil storage areas
  • A concrete or impervious floor with diking is required to prevent stormwater and rainfall contact
  • Immediately clean up spills of used oil with absorbents and properly dispose of the spent materials

slides.title: Transportation of Used Oil
slides.description:
• Used oil shipped off site must be picked up by transporters with EPA ID numbers
  • This applies to filters and oily rags
  • Keep logs or records of off-site shipments of used oil

slides.title: Mixing Other Materials with Used Oil
slides.description:
Only other materials defined as used oil may be mixed with used oil, examples:

  • Transmission and hydraulic fluids
  • Petroleum-based, non-hazardous lubricating fluids
  • Hydraulic, cutting, gear and cooling oils
  • Synthetic oils

Never mix gasoline, wastewater, a listed hazardous waste, an unknown waste, halogenated solvents or antifreeze with used oil.

slides.title: Used Oil Filter Disposal/Recycling
slides.description:
Only other materials defined as used oil may be mixed with used oil, examples:

  • Over 400 million used oil filters are generated in the US a year To be disposed of, they must be properly treated.
  • Recycling of used filters is becoming more common
  • Used oil filters are generally picked up by an EPA certified contractor and:
    • Shredded, cut open and solvent washed
    • Crushed into low-density pucks
    • Crushed into high-density briquettes
    • Burned directly in cement kilns
    • Recycled as scrap steel
    • Prepared for acceptable landfilling

questions.question: Which of the following is required when storing used oil?

answers.b: Containers/tanks must be leak-proof, closed when not in use, and labeled “Used Oil”
answers.c: Store used oil in any available bins
answers.d: Label containers only if they are outdoors

questions.question: Used oil storage areas should display “No Smoking” signs.
How often should weekly checks be performed for leaks, corrosion, or spills in used oil storage areas?
Used oil may be stored in units other than tanks or containers if they are strong enough.
Which materials are acceptable to mix with used oil?

answers.c: Transmission fluids, hydraulic fluids, and petroleum-based lubricants

questions.question: Used oil must be transported by:

answers.a: Any employee with a pickup truck
answers.b: EPA State-certified transporters (and records must be maintained)
answers.d: Anyone as long as the containers are sealed

questions.question: A facility may fall under SPCC rules if it has more than 1,320 gallons of aboveground oil storage and there is a chance oil could reach U.S. waters or drainage systems.
